disease_context: TP53 is mutated in over 50% of all human cancers, acting as the 'guardian of the genome'. Loss of p53 function allows cells to bypass apoptosis and accumulate oncogenic mutations.
difficulty_rationale: Intrinsically disordered N- and C-termini, large flat protein-protein interaction surface, no deep binding pockets; most small-molecule approaches target the DNA-binding domain mutant restoration.

known_drugs.name: APR-246 (Eprenetapopt)
known_drugs.mechanism: Converts mutant p53 to wild-type-like conformation, restoring apoptosis

known_drugs.name: AMG 232
known_drugs.mechanism: MDM2 inhibitor releasing p53 from negative regulation

disease_context: BRCA1 is a tumour suppressor involved in DNA double-strand break repair via homologous recombination. Germline mutations dramatically increase lifetime risk of breast and ovarian cancer.
difficulty_rationale: Large multi-domain scaffold protein; therapeutic strategy focuses on synthetic lethality (PARP inhibitors) rather than direct BRCA1 targeting. Very few druggable pockets on the protein itself.

known_drugs.name: Olaparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP inhibitor exploiting BRCA1 deficiency via synthetic lethality

known_drugs.name: Niraparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 inhibitor, approved for BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer

known_drugs.name: Talazoparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP inhibitor with PARP trapping activity

disease_context: EGFR is overexpressed or mutated in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), colorectal, and head/neck cancers. Activating mutations in exons 19-21 drive kinase-dependent proliferation.
difficulty_rationale: Well-validated kinase target with a defined ATP-binding pocket. Resistance mutations (T790M, C797S) complicate drug design but multiple generations of inhibitors have been developed.

known_drugs.name: Erlotinib
known_drugs.mechanism: First-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), reversible ATP-competitive

known_drugs.name: Osimertinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Third-generation TKI targeting T790M resistance mutation, covalent C797

known_drugs.name: Cetuximab
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody blocking ligand binding

disease_context: HER2 (ERBB2) is amplified in ~20% of breast cancers and gastric cancers, driving aggressive tumour growth. HER2-positive breast cancer has poor prognosis without targeted therapy.
difficulty_rationale: Well-characterised kinase domain; multiple approved drugs. Main challenge is identifying molecules that overcome lapatinib/trastuzumab resistance and CNS penetration.

known_drugs.name: Trastuzumab (Herceptin)
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody, blocks extracellular domain IV

known_drugs.name: Pertuzumab
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-HER2 antibody blocking domain II dimerisation

disease_context: KRAS is the most frequently mutated oncogene in human cancer (~25% overall), particularly pancreatic (90%), colorectal (40%), and lung cancers (30%). G12C, G12D, and G12V mutations lock KRAS in the active GTP-bound state.
difficulty_rationale: Historically considered 'undruggable' due to picomolar GTP affinity and featureless surface. The G12C covalent pocket discovery was a breakthrough, but G12D/G12V remain extremely difficult.

known_drugs.name: Sotorasib (AMG510)
known_drugs.mechanism: First covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor, locks in GDP-bound inactive state

disease_context: BCL2 is an anti-apoptotic protein overexpressed in follicular lymphoma (t(14;18) translocation), CLL, and many solid tumours. It sequesters pro-apoptotic proteins BIM, BAX, and BAK to block programmed cell death.
difficulty_rationale: BH3-binding hydrophobic groove is a validated drug target. Venetoclax demonstrates proof-of-concept; main challenge is selectivity among BCL2 family members (BCL-XL, MCL1).

known_drugs.name: Venetoclax (ABT-199)
known_drugs.mechanism: BH3 mimetic selectively targeting BCL2, displaces pro-apoptotic BIM

disease_context: CDK4 partners with cyclin D1 to phosphorylate RB1 and drive G1→S cell cycle progression. Amplified in ~15% of cancers (liposarcoma, breast, lung); constitutively active CDK4/6 enables uncontrolled proliferation.
difficulty_rationale: Deep, well-defined ATP-binding pocket with good selectivity features. Multiple approved drugs demonstrate high tractability. Main challenge is selectivity over CDK6.

known_drugs.name: Palbociclib (Ibrance)
known_drugs.mechanism: Selective CDK4/6 inhibitor, arrests cell cycle at G1

known_drugs.name: Ribociclib (Kisqali)
known_drugs.mechanism: CDK4/6 inhibitor for HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer

known_drugs.name: Abemaciclib (Verzenio)
known_drugs.mechanism: CDK4/6 inhibitor with greater CDK4 selectivity

disease_context: VEGFR2 (KDR) is the primary mediator of VEGF-driven tumour angiogenesis. Solid tumours upregulate VEGF to recruit new blood vessels; blocking VEGFR2 starves the tumour of nutrients and oxygen.
difficulty_rationale: Well-validated kinase target with approved multi-kinase inhibitors. Selectivity over other VEGFR family members and off-target kinases (PDGFR, c-Kit) is the key design challenge.

known_drugs.name: Sorafenib
known_drugs.mechanism: RAF/VEGFR2/PDGFR TKI blocking angiogenesis and proliferation

disease_context: PD-L1 is expressed on tumour cells and tumour-associated macrophages to suppress anti-tumour T-cell immunity via PD-1 engagement. Checkpoint inhibition targeting PD-L1 has revolutionised treatment of melanoma, NSCLC, and many other cancers.
difficulty_rationale: IgV-like domain has a well-characterised CC' loop binding interface for PD-1. Small-molecule disruptors of the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction have been developed and entered clinical trials, validating druggability.

known_drugs.name: Atezolizumab (Tecentriq)
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody blocking PD-1/PD-L1 interaction

known_drugs.name: Durvalumab (Imfinzi)
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 antibody, also blocks CD80 interaction

known_drugs.name: Avelumab (Bavencio)
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 IgG1 antibody with ADCC activity

disease_context: MDM2 is the principal negative regulator of p53, targeting it for proteasomal degradation. MDM2 is amplified in ~7% of all cancers (especially liposarcoma and osteosarcoma), enabling tumour cells to silence p53.
difficulty_rationale: The p53-binding hydrophobic cleft on MDM2 is one of the best characterised protein-protein interaction drug targets. Multiple clinical-stage inhibitors with sub-nanomolar affinity have been developed.

known_drugs.name: Idasanutlin (RG7388)
known_drugs.mechanism: Potent selective MDM2 antagonist, displaces p53 Phe19/Trp23/Leu26 triad

known_drugs.name: Milademetan (DS-3032b)
known_drugs.mechanism: MDM2 inhibitor with broad solid tumour activity

disease_context: BRAF is mutated in approximately 50% of melanomas (predominantly V600E), 10–15% of colorectal cancers, and multiple other tumour types. The V600E substitution constitutively activates the MAPK/ERK signalling cascade, driving unchecked cellular proliferation.
difficulty_rationale: V600E mutation creates an oncogenic kinase; achieving selectivity over other RAF family members and overcoming gatekeeper resistance mutations requires precise pocket engineering. Paradoxical MAPK pathway activation with pan-RAF inhibitors adds complexity.

known_drugs.name: Encorafenib
known_drugs.mechanism: Next-generation BRAF V600E inhibitor with extended target residence time

protein_name: Phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphatase and dual-specificity protein phosphatase PTEN
disease_context: PTEN is lost or mutated in over 30% of all human cancers including glioblastoma, prostate, breast, and endometrial cancers. It is a major negative regulator of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway; its loss leads to constitutive pro-survival signalling.
difficulty_rationale: PTEN is a tumour suppressor — most cancers involve its loss-of-function, making traditional small-molecule inhibition counterproductive; therapeutic strategies aim at restoring PTEN function or exploiting synthetic lethality. No approved direct inhibitor exists, and the shallow phosphatase active site is difficult to target selectively.

known_drugs.name: PACLITAXEL (synthetic lethality context)
known_drugs.mechanism: Exploits PTEN-loss-driven genomic instability via mitotic arrest

known_drugs.name: GSK2636771 (investigational)
known_drugs.mechanism: PI3Kβ inhibitor exploiting PTEN-deficient synthetic lethality

disease_context: MYC is amplified or overexpressed in approximately 70% of all human cancers. It drives transcription of hundreds of genes involved in cell-cycle progression, protein synthesis, and metabolism. Considered 'undruggable' for decades; recent PROTAC and bHLH-LZ disruption strategies are early-stage.
difficulty_rationale: MYC is an intrinsically disordered transcription factor with no defined small-molecule binding pocket in the canonical sense. It acts as a scaffold for large multi-protein complexes; the only tractable approach is disrupting MYC-MAX heterodimerisation via the bHLH-LZ domain, but the interaction surface is flat and high-affinity inhibitors have proven extremely challenging to develop.

known_drugs.name: OMOMYC (biologics)
known_drugs.mechanism: Dominant-negative MYC bHLH-LZ construct disrupting MYC-MAX dimerisation

protein_name: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3
disease_context: STAT3 is constitutively activated in many cancers including breast, lung, prostate, and haematological malignancies. It mediates tumour immune evasion by promoting immunosuppressive cytokine production and is a master regulator of cancer stem-cell maintenance.
difficulty_rationale: STAT3 SH2 domain mediates protein-protein interactions with a relatively flat surface; disrupting it with drug-like small molecules with selectivity over STAT1/5 has proved difficult. No approved direct STAT3 inhibitor exists; most clinical attempts have failed due to poor potency or selectivity.

known_drugs.name: Napabucasin (investigational)
known_drugs.mechanism: STAT3 transcriptional activity inhibitor / reactive oxygen species generator

known_drugs.name: TTI-101 (investigational)
known_drugs.mechanism: Selective SH2 domain phosphopeptide mimetic inhibitor

disease_context: PIK3CA is one of the most frequently mutated oncogenes in human cancer, altered in approximately 30% of breast cancers, 20% of colorectal cancers, and multiple other tumour types. Hotspot mutations (H1047R, E545K, E542K) constitutively activate the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.
difficulty_rationale: The PI3Kα ATP-binding site is well-defined but achieving isoform selectivity over PI3Kβ/δ/γ requires subtle structural differentiation. Gaining alpha-isoform selectivity was the key challenge solved by alpelisib; resistance mutations (H1047R, E545K) shift binding dynamics.

disease_context: mTOR is a central integrator of growth factor, nutrient, and energy signals, dysregulated in RCC, breast cancer, neuroendocrine tumours, and TSC-related tumours. mTORC1/mTORC2 complexes regulate protein synthesis, autophagy, and cellular metabolism downstream of PI3K/AKT.
difficulty_rationale: mTOR is a large (~289 kDa) multi-domain PIKK-family kinase. Achieving selectivity over PI3K family members is achievable; the FRB domain provides an allosteric handle for rapamycin analogues. Resistance via S2035I gatekeeper and feedback activation of AKT limit single-agent utility.

disease_context: FGFR1 is amplified or mutated in bladder cancer (FGFR3 predominantly), lung squamous cell carcinoma, and multiple myeloma. FGFR gene fusions and point mutations drive constitutive kinase activation in multiple tumour types.
difficulty_rationale: FGFR1 kinase domain has a well-druggable ATP pocket, but achieving selectivity across the four FGFR paralogs (FGFR1-4) required careful medicinal chemistry. Off-target VEGFR inhibition caused toxicities with early pan-FGFR agents; hyperphosphatemia is an on-target adverse effect unique to FGFR inhibition.

disease_context: RET gene fusions (KIF5B-RET, CCDC6-RET) are drivers in 1–2% of NSCLC and point mutations (C634, M918T) are found in 95% of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). RET is among the first targets where precision oncology enabled highly selective therapeutic development.
difficulty_rationale: RET is a receptor tyrosine kinase with an accessible ATP-binding pocket. First-generation multi-kinase inhibitors had off-target toxicities; selective RET inhibitors required structure-guided design to distinguish RET from VEGFR2 (similar binding site geometry). Solvent-front resistance mutations (G810) remain clinically relevant.

disease_context: The androgen receptor drives prostate cancer proliferation through testosterone and DHT binding. Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) develops when tumours reactivate AR signalling despite androgen deprivation, representing the major cause of prostate cancer mortality.
difficulty_rationale: The androgen receptor LBD is well-characterised and highly druggable; challenges arise from resistance mechanisms including LBD mutations (F876L, T877A), constitutively active splice variants (AR-V7 lacking LBD), and glucocorticoid receptor bypass. N-terminal domain targeting and AR degraders represent next-generation approaches.

known_drugs.name: Enzalutamide
known_drugs.mechanism: Second-generation AR antagonist with no agonist switch

known_drugs.name: Darolutamide
known_drugs.mechanism: Structurally distinct AR antagonist with low CNS penetration

protein_name: High affinity nerve growth factor receptor
disease_context: NTRK1 gene fusions (ETV6-NTRK3, TPM3-NTRK1, others) are rare but highly druggable pan-cancer drivers found in diverse tumour types including secretory breast cancer, infantile fibrosarcoma, lung, and colon cancers. Larotrectinib showed >75% overall response rate across 17 tumour types in basket trial — one of the first tumour-agnostic approvals.
difficulty_rationale: NTRK1 kinase domain has a tractable, well-defined ATP-binding cleft and high similarity across the NTRK family, enabling pan-TRK inhibitors with broad efficacy. Type I DFG-in inhibitors like larotrectinib achieve picomolar potency; resistance mutations (G595R, G667C) are addressable with second-generation inhibitors.

known_drugs.name: Selitrectinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Second-generation TRK inhibitor targeting G595R resistance

disease_context: IDH1 is mutated (R132H/C/G/L/S) in 80% of low-grade gliomas and secondary glioblastomas, and 15-20% of AML cases. Mutant IDH1 produces 2-hydroxyglutarate, an oncometabolite that blocks cell differentiation and drives epigenetic dysregulation.
difficulty_rationale: Allosteric binding pocket in mutant IDH1 is well-defined but requires selectivity over wild-type IDH1 and IDH2. High-affinity binding with precise hydrogen bond geometry to R132H required.

disease_context: FLT3 is mutated in ~30% of AML cases (ITD mutations in 25% and TKD mutations in 7%). FLT3-ITD confers poor prognosis with high relapse rates. FLT3 drives leukemic cell proliferation and survival through constitutive activation.
difficulty_rationale: Must overcome resistance mutations (D835Y/H/N, F691L) that emerge under inhibitor pressure. ITD-specific conformational changes complicate structure-based design. Selectivity over KIT and PDGFR required.

disease_context: SMAD4 is lost in 55% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (among the most lethal cancers with <12% 5-year survival) and 15% of colorectal cancers. SMAD4 loss abolishes TGF-β tumor suppression, enabling invasion and metastasis.
difficulty_rationale: Tumor suppressor — loss-of-function mutations require restoration strategies rather than inhibition. No approved inhibitor exists. PPI surface targeting the MH2 domain is structurally challenging.

known_drugs.name: None approved
known_drugs.mechanism: No approved small-molecule inhibitor — tumor suppressor restoration under investigation

disease_context: APC is the most commonly mutated gene in colorectal cancer (80% of sporadic cases) and familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). APC loss constitutively activates WNT/β-catenin signalling, driving uncontrolled proliferation. APC mutations are early, founder events in colon carcinogenesis.
difficulty_rationale: Very large multi-domain scaffold protein (2843 aa); tumor suppressor requiring restoration not inhibition. No small molecule binding pocket confirmed by crystallography. WNT pathway modulation via indirect targets is the current approach.

known_drugs.name: None approved
known_drugs.mechanism: No approved small-molecule inhibitor — tumor suppressor restoration under investigation

disease_context: PARP1 is a master regulator of DNA damage repair. Inhibition is synthetically lethal in BRCA1/2-deficient tumors (ovarian, breast, pancreatic, prostate cancers). PARP trapping — where the inhibitor locks PARP onto damaged DNA — is the key cytotoxic mechanism.
difficulty_rationale: Well-characterized NAD+-binding catalytic domain with multiple approved inhibitors. Differentiation requires PARP trapping potency and selectivity over PARP2. Resistance via PARP1 mutations (D770N, P882S) emerging in clinic.

known_drugs.name: Olaparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 inhibitor; NAD+ mimetic with trapping

disease_context: JAK2 V617F mutation is found in >95% of polycythemia vera and 50-60% of essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis cases. JAK2 signaling through STAT3/5 drives cytokine-independent proliferation of hematopoietic progenitors.
difficulty_rationale: ATP-competitive kinase with pseudo-kinase JH2 domain. V617F gain-of-function mutation in JH2 relieves autoinhibition. Selectivity over JAK1/3 is important to minimize immunosuppression. Type II inhibitors targeting the DFG-out conformation show promise.

disease_context: ESR1 drives ~70% of breast cancers (ER-positive). Endocrine therapy is first-line treatment, but ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations (Y537S, D538G) emerge in 30-40% of metastatic cases, conferring resistance to aromatase inhibitors and tamoxifen.
difficulty_rationale: Well-characterized ligand-binding domain with multiple co-crystal structures. Challenge: designing molecules that degrade rather than merely inhibit ER (PROTAC or SERD approach), and overcoming resistance mutations Y537S and D538G.

known_drugs.name: Elacestrant
known_drugs.mechanism: Oral SERD; active against ESR1 mutations

disease_context: HDAC1 is overexpressed in multiple cancer types (lung, colon, gastric, breast, prostate). HDAC1 in the NuRD and Sin3A co-repressor complexes silences tumor suppressor genes via histone deacetylation. HDAC1 inhibition restores p21, p27, and BAX expression, inducing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
difficulty_rationale: Zinc-dependent enzyme with canonical catalytic tunnel. Class-selective inhibitors (HDAC1/2 vs HDAC3/6/8) require precise metal-chelating warhead geometry. Resistance via compensatory HDAC2 upregulation. Isoform selectivity reduces cardiac toxicity.

disease_context: HDAC2 is overexpressed in colorectal, gastric, and cervical cancers. HDAC2 selective inhibition shows particular promise in Alzheimer's disease (memory improvement in preclinical models) and cancers with HDAC2 amplification. HDAC2 is 87% identical to HDAC1, making isoform-selective targeting a major challenge.
difficulty_rationale: Near-identical active site to HDAC1 (87% sequence identity). Selective inhibition requires exploitation of subtle surface differences near the catalytic tunnel rim. Combination with PD-1 inhibitors shows synergy in solid tumors.

known_drugs.name: Romidepsin
known_drugs.mechanism: Bicyclic depsipeptide; class I HDAC inhibitor

disease_context: BCR-ABL1 fusion (Philadelphia chromosome) drives >95% of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and 25-30% of adult B-ALL. Imatinib (Gleevec) was the first molecularly targeted cancer drug and transformed CML from a fatal disease to a manageable chronic condition with >90% 10-year survival. ABL1 remains the blueprint for kinase inhibitor drug discovery.
difficulty_rationale: Multiple resistance mutations (T315I gatekeeper, E255K/V, Y253H) require pan-resistant inhibitors. Third-generation inhibitors (ponatinib, asciminib) target the myristoyl pocket allosterically. STAMP mechanism (allosteric + ATP competitive) is state-of-the-art.

known_drugs.name: Asciminib
known_drugs.mechanism: STAMP inhibitor; targets ABL1 myristoyl pocket

disease_context: MYC is overexpressed or amplified in ~70% of all cancers. Small molecules targeting the MYC mRNA IRES or 5'-CDS stem-loop block ribosome loading, reducing MYC protein without targeting the undruggable MYC protein surface directly.
difficulty_rationale: mRNA IRES elements are highly structured but poorly crystallised; few validated small-molecule binders exist. Scoring relies on computational RNA docking (affinity proxy). Hard tier reflects frontier science status.

disease_context: KRAS is the most commonly mutated oncogene in pancreatic, lung, and colon cancers. Targeting KRAS mRNA blocks expression upstream of the protein, circumventing the challenging nucleotide-binding pocket.
difficulty_rationale: KRAS mRNA lacks a well-characterised IRES; the 5'-CDS forms a labile stem-loop. RNA-targeted small molecules for KRAS are at early research stage.

disease_context: BCL2 mRNA contains a well-characterised IRES that allows cap-independent translation under stress. Blocking BCL2 IRES with small molecules reduces the anti-apoptotic protein load in lymphoma and CLL cells.
difficulty_rationale: BCL2 IRES is one of the best-studied cancer mRNA IRESes; several compounds have been tested in vitro. Moderate structural data available.

disease_context: EGFR is overexpressed or mutated in non-small-cell lung cancer, head and neck cancer, and glioblastoma. Blocking EGFR mRNA translation at the 5'-CDS provides a route around kinase-domain resistance mutations.
difficulty_rationale: EGFR mRNA 5'-UTR is GC-rich with complex folding; identifying a selective small-molecule binding pocket requires computational RNA structure prediction.

disease_context: HER2 is amplified in 20-30% of breast cancers and gastric cancers. mRNA-level silencing bypasses trastuzumab resistance caused by downstream PI3K/AKT mutations.
difficulty_rationale: HER2 mRNA 5'-UTR IRES has been partially characterised; no approved mRNA-targeted compounds exist. High novelty, hard tier.

disease_context: BRAF V600E mutation drives ~50% of melanomas and ~10% of colorectal cancers. Targeting BRAF mRNA prevents V600E protein production independent of the mutation status of the kinase domain.
difficulty_rationale: Novel mRNA silencing modality; minimal structural data on BRAF mRNA.

disease_context: MDM2 negatively regulates p53 by promoting its ubiquitination. Blocking MDM2 mRNA translation restores p53 tumour suppressor activity in cancers with wild-type p53 but MDM2 amplification.
difficulty_rationale: MDM2 mRNA contains an IRES that is upregulated after DNA damage; selective IRES inhibitors are a frontier area.

disease_context: CDK4 drives G1/S cell-cycle entry; it is amplified or overactivated in breast, liposarcoma, and glioblastoma. mRNA-level blockade complements CDK4/6 kinase inhibitors by preventing de novo protein synthesis.
difficulty_rationale: No characterised mRNA-binding compounds; highly novel.

disease_context: Cyclin D1 (CCND1) is overexpressed in breast, head/neck, oesophageal, and mantle cell lymphoma. Its mRNA 3'UTR AU-rich element is a validated target for mRNA stability modulation by small molecules.
difficulty_rationale: AU-rich elements are single-stranded and conformationally flexible; small-molecule binding requires structure-specific ligands.

protein_name: Baculoviral IAP repeat-containing protein 5 / Survivin (mRNA target)
disease_context: Survivin is expressed in virtually all cancer types but absent in normal adult tissues. It inhibits apoptosis and regulates mitosis. Its mRNA IRES is active during mitosis, making it a cell-cycle-specific RNA target.
difficulty_rationale: Survivin mRNA IRES is among the better-studied cancer IRESes. Several compounds have been screened in IRES reporter assays; none approved.
known_binders: YM155 (transcription inhibitor, not direct mRNA binder)

disease_context: PD-L1 (CD274) expressed on tumour cells suppresses cytotoxic T-cell responses. Small molecules targeting PD-L1 mRNA stability elements in the 3'UTR could reduce tumour immune evasion without antibody-class therapeutics.
difficulty_rationale: 3'UTR elements are single-stranded; selectivity over other immune checkpoint mRNAs is challenging.

protein_name: Vascular endothelial growth factor A (mRNA target)
mrna_region: 5'UTR IRES (two IRES elements, A and B)
disease_context: VEGF-A mRNA contains two IRESes (IRES-A and IRES-B) that drive cap-independent translation under hypoxia—a hallmark of solid tumours. IRES-targeting compounds could suppress tumour angiogenesis selectively under hypoxic conditions where conventional anti-VEGF antibodies are less effective.
difficulty_rationale: VEGF IRES is among the best-characterised cancer mRNA IRESes; moderate structural data.

disease_context: HIF-1α protein is stabilised under tumour hypoxia and drives transcription of pro-survival and pro-angiogenic genes. HIF1A mRNA harbours an IRES active under hypoxic conditions, providing a cancer-selective RNA target.
difficulty_rationale: HIF1A IRES has been characterised; some small-molecule screens published.

disease_context: IL-6 promotes tumour growth, immune evasion, and cachexia. Its mRNA is post-transcriptionally regulated by AU-rich elements (AREs) in the 3'UTR. Small molecules stabilising the ARE or blocking ARE-binding proteins reduce IL-6 production in cancer and inflammation.
difficulty_rationale: AREs are unstructured; selectivity across cytokine mRNAs is the main challenge.
known_binders: Thalidomide (indirect, destabilises TNF/IL-6 mRNA via CELF)

disease_context: TNF plays dual roles in cancer: anti-tumour at high concentrations but pro-tumour chronically. TNF mRNA ARE is a validated therapeutic target; thalidomide-class drugs destabilise TNF mRNA. Novel direct ARE binders are sought for improved selectivity.
difficulty_rationale: TNF ARE is the founding model of mRNA destabilisation; several compound classes known.

disease_context: TGF-β1 suppresses anti-tumour immune responses and promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Its mRNA 5'UTR contains a translational control element (TCE) that governs cap-dependent translation; blocking the TCE reduces TGF-β1 secretion by tumour-associated cells.
difficulty_rationale: TGFb1 mRNA TCE is structured but incompletely characterised at atomic resolution.

disease_context: CSF1R drives differentiation of tumour-associated macrophages (TAMs), which suppress anti-tumour immunity. Blocking CSF1R mRNA reduces TAM recruitment without systemic immunosuppression.
difficulty_rationale: Novel mRNA target; no published mRNA-binding compounds.

disease_context: CCL2 recruits immunosuppressive monocytes and TAMs to the tumour microenvironment. Its mRNA 3'UTR ARE governs stability; small-molecule destabilisers could reduce CCL2-mediated immune suppression.
difficulty_rationale: ARE targeting; selectivity among chemokine mRNAs required.

disease_context: CXCL12/SDF-1 guides cancer cell migration to metastatic niches via CXCR4. Blocking CXCL12 mRNA production reduces metastatic seeding in breast, prostate, and haematological cancers.
difficulty_rationale: Novel mRNA target for metastasis; no characterised RNA binders.

disease_context: MMP9 degrades extracellular matrix to enable tumour invasion and metastasis. Blocking MMP9 mRNA at the 5'-CDS junction reduces secreted MMP9 activity in aggressive cancers.
difficulty_rationale: Novel RNA target modality for MMP9; highly innovative.

disease_context: LDHA drives the Warburg effect by converting pyruvate to lactate, supporting aerobic glycolysis in cancer. LDHA mRNA is upregulated by HIF-1α. mRNA-level silencing reduces the metabolic advantage of cancer cells without affecting normal tissue LDHB.
difficulty_rationale: Metabolic mRNA target; isoform selectivity (LDHA vs LDHB) is key challenge.

protein_name: Pyruvate kinase PKM, isoform M2 (mRNA target)
mrna_region: Exon 10 inclusion regulatory element (alternative splicing target)
disease_context: PKM2 (vs PKM1) is selectively expressed in cancer cells and supports biosynthesis over ATP generation. Small molecules targeting the PKM2-specific exon 10 splicing regulatory element could switch PKM2 to PKM1, reversing the Warburg effect.
difficulty_rationale: Splicing regulatory elements are poorly drugged; highly innovative modality.

protein_name: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 1 (mRNA target)
disease_context: GLUT1 (SLC2A1) is the primary glucose transporter upregulated in cancer cells via HIF-1α. Blocking GLUT1 mRNA translation selectively in hypoxic tumour cells starves cancer of its preferred energy source.
difficulty_rationale: HIF-responsive mRNA elements are partially characterised; isoform selectivity required.

disease_context: HK2 is the cancer-specific hexokinase that phosphorylates glucose as the first committed step of glycolysis. HK2 is absent in most normal adult tissues but highly expressed in cancer. mRNA targeting provides tumour selectivity.
difficulty_rationale: Cancer-selective expression makes HK2 mRNA an attractive target; no known RNA binders.

disease_context: FASN drives de novo lipogenesis in cancer cells for membrane biosynthesis and energy storage. FASN is overexpressed in breast, prostate, and colorectal cancers. mRNA silencing reduces fatty acid synthesis selectively in lipogenic tumours.
difficulty_rationale: FASN mRNA lacks well-characterised RNA structures; highly novel target.

disease_context: TERT is the catalytic subunit of telomerase, reactivated in >90% of cancers to confer immortality. TERT mRNA contains a G-quadruplex structure in the 5'UTR that suppresses translation; G-quadruplex stabilisers reduce TERT protein levels selectively in cancer cells.
difficulty_rationale: TERT mRNA G-quadruplex is well-characterised (NMR structure available). Several G-quadruplex ligands have been tested in vitro. One of the more tractable mRNA RNA targets in this set.

disease_context: PARP1 performs DNA single-strand break repair essential for cancer cell survival after genotoxic stress. Blocking PARP1 mRNA translation is an alternative modality to PARP inhibitors that avoids the resistance mechanism of PARP trapping reversal.
difficulty_rationale: Novel mRNA modality for PARP1; existing PARP inhibitors target the protein.

disease_context: RAD51 mediates homologous recombination repair, allowing cancer cells to survive DNA-damaging chemotherapy. Blocking RAD51 mRNA translation sensitises BRCA-proficient tumours to PARP inhibitors and platinum drugs (synthetic lethality extension).
difficulty_rationale: High therapeutic rationale; no validated mRNA binders published.

protein_name: Breast cancer type 2 susceptibility protein (mRNA target)
disease_context: BRCA2 mediates homologous recombination; its loss creates PARP-inhibitor sensitivity. In tumours with wild-type BRCA2, blocking BRCA2 mRNA translation creates de novo synthetic lethality, extending PARP inhibitor utility to a broader patient population.
difficulty_rationale: Synthetic lethality via mRNA; no prior art in RNA-targeted BRCA2 modulation.

disease_context: ATM orchestrates the DNA damage response checkpoint. Blocking ATM mRNA translation abrogates the G2/M checkpoint, forcing cancer cells into premature mitosis after DNA damage—a radio/chemo-sensitisation strategy independent of kinase-domain ATM inhibitors.
difficulty_rationale: Novel mRNA-level checkpoint abrogation; no RNA-binding compounds known for ATM.
